key_insight: Aggregate validation metrics (e.g., perplexity) hide diverse downstream scaling behaviors—some tasks improve, some plateau, and some degrade as models scale—so predicting task performance requires finer-grained, flexible analysis rather than a single power-law fit.
problem_solved: Clarifies why downstream performance is poorly predicted from validation perplexity by identifying two failure modes: averaging token-level losses obscures actionable signal, and no simple parametric family universally captures the heterogeneous scaling trajectories of individual tasks.
method: Empirical analysis of downstream task performance across model scales to characterize distinct scaling regimes (monotonic improvement, plateau, degradation).
Decompose aggregate validation loss into finer-grained signals (per-task / per-example / per-token) to reveal predictive structure lost by averaging.
Introduce flexible, nonparametric or mixture-style modeling and evaluation protocols to fit and forecast diverse task-specific scaling curves.
impact: Enables practitioners to better forecast how specific tasks will respond to increased compute or model size, choose evaluation metrics beyond perplexity, and make more cost-effective scaling decisions for downstream objectives.
visual_elements: Line plot with multiple exemplar task curves showing monotonic improvement, plateauing, and degradation across model scale.
Heatmap or violin plots of per-token or per-example loss distributions at different scales to show where averaging hides signal.
Schematic pipeline: aggregate loss → decomposition → flexible fit → downstream performance prediction.
Icon set emphasizing pitfalls (magnifying glass over 'perplexity', warning triangle) and recommendations (scaling budget, task-specific evaluation checklist).
paper_authors: Michael Y. Hu, Jane Pan, Ayush Rajesh Jhaveri, Nicholas Lourie, Kyunghyun Cho
